brief.headline: Push for ₹3.37 L savings by matching our best LDPE bottle price, leveraging our 7.21% revenue share and their urgent need for cash.

priceAsk.summary: Reduce LDPE BOTTLE 5ML WHITE OPAQUE from ₹1.69/NOS to ₹1.62/NOS to match our best price
priceAsk.target: ₹1.62/NOS — the price we pay Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited — saving ₹3.37 L annually
priceAsk.basis: We currently pay them ₹1.69/NOS, a 4.3% gap above the ₹1.62/NOS best price we already secure elsewhere; closing this gap eliminates ₹3.37 L in annual excess cost

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 Days After Receipt; offer accelerated payment only in exchange for the full price reduction
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Extending by 15 days would free ₹3.34 L working capital for us, but they need cash more — use faster payment as a sweetener if they resist the price cut

brief.financialLeverage: Berry Global India is loss-making with a -199.2% net margin versus 2.3% peer median, EBITDA margin of -87.3%, and a Probe42 financial score of 1/10. They carry debt of 220.44x equity and an interest coverage of -3.71x. Our ₹81.39 L annual spend represents 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr revenue — we are a material customer they cannot afford to lose. Their 335d cash conversion cycle (versus 70d peer median) and 226d payable days (versus 41d peer median) signal acute cash stress. They value speed and volume certainty over margin, so we can press hard on price but must offer payment speed or volume commitment in return, and keep alternates ready given the supply-continuity risk.

evidence.point: We pay them 4.3% more than our best supplier for the same LDPE bottle
evidence.figure: Gap: 4.3%, our price ₹1.69/NOS vs best price ₹1.62/NOS

evidence.point: Closing the price gap saves us ₹3.37 L per year
We represent over 7% of their total revenue, giving us negotiating weight
They are deeply unprofitable, running a net margin nearly 200 percentage points below peers
Their cash cycle is nearly five times the peer median, indicating severe working-capital strain
evidence.figure: Cash conversion cycle 335d vs peer median 70d

evidence.point: Extreme leverage and negative interest coverage flag financial distress

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter with pharma bottles, caps and preforms capability — top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader serving pharma with strong health score (A) — a robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed supplier with moulded and blow-moulded packaging capability across bottles and caps

risks: They are loss-making (PAT ₹-22.50 Cr in FY2023-24) with a 1/10 Probe42 score — deep price cuts risk supply disruption; keep Manjushree or Mold-Tek warm
High leverage (220.44x debt-to-equity) and negative margins mean they may walk away rather than accept unsustainable pricing; be ready to offer volume commitment or faster payment as a trade
Our ₹81.39 L spend is 7.21% of their revenue — losing us would hurt them materially, but their financial fragility means they might choose survival over our business
Their 335d cash cycle and -87.3% EBITDA margin indicate they are burning cash; if they fail, we have no immediate backup on this SKU — dual-source now
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹1.69 per unit when we know ₹1.62 is achievable — let's close that gap and talk about how we can help your cash flow in return.
